title: fix(metadata): a removal reaches a cluster peer's artifact-door copy too, so a removed item stops answering on every node
body:
Fixes #32499

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：集群里一个节点注销元数据（`unregister` / `unregisterPackage` / `bulkUnregister`）时，广播给其他节点的 `deleted` 消息带上一个 `removal` 标记（含被删条目所属的包）；其他节点收到后也删掉自己内存里产物门加载的那份副本，而不仅是注册表条目。
- 为什么改：之前执行注销的节点不再返回该条目，其他节点却继续从自己的产物门内存副本返回它，各节点对“这个条目还在不在”说法不一。
- 风险与回滚：只在收到带 `removal` 标记的删除消息时动内存副本；更新、文件/仓库监听产生的删除、旧版本节点发来的消息都不碰。对端从不重复删共享数据库。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts` 的 `attachClusterPubSub` 接收处与新增的 `removeNodeLocalCopies`；`ClusterMetadataChangedPayload.removal` 的文档注释；`metadata-manager-cluster.test.ts` 末尾新增的 #32499 describe。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/metadata-manager-cluster.test.ts`，预期 44 例全过。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`MetadataManager.unregister` deletes the artifact door's in-memory (`memory:`) copy of a removed item on the node that runs it (#32493). A cluster peer heard the removal on `metadata.changed` and ran `invalidateForForeignWrite`, which drops only the registry entry and the list cache, so its next read fell through to its own door `MemoryLoader` and served the removed item.

- `packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts`
  - `ClusterMetadataChangedPayload` gains an optional `removal: { packageId? }`. The type is module-internal (not re-exported from the package index). Only `unregisterAt`'s `deleted` announcement sets it, with the same `packageId` its own loader deletes used, through a new optional third parameter of `notifyWatchers`. The watcher event itself is unchanged: the spec's `MetadataWatchEvent` declares no package (the `⛔` constraint in `unregisterAt`).
  - On receipt, before `invalidateForForeignWrite`, a payload whose `removal` reads cleanly starts `removeNodeLocalCopies(type, name, packageId)`. That method deletes from the node-local loaders only, through the same `deleteMetaItemFromLoader` the acting node uses. Then it drops the list cache once more, for a loader whose delete is genuinely asynchronous.
  - `isRemovalTarget` is split. Its `memory:` half becomes `isNodeLocalRemovalTarget`, so the acting node and the peer share one spelling. The peer never deletes from the shared `datasource:` store: the origin already did, and a second delete could take out a row written again in between.
  - `receivedRemovalOf` drops a `removal` whose `packageId` is not a string. Read as a by-name removal, it would delete wider than the origin did.
  - A peer whose in-memory loader refuses the delete logs once at `error`, naming the consequence and the fix (AGENTS.md "Degradation log levels").
- Mechanism choice, measured: the PM's note held. `invalidateForForeignWrite` runs for create, update and nameless events, and also for `deleted` events that are not removals. `NodeMetadataManager`'s file `unlink` and `applyRepoEvent`'s repository delete both call `notifyWatchers`, which publishes on the cluster channel, but neither deletes the origin's door copy. So keying the drop on `event.type === 'deleted'` would have made peers diverge the other way. The drop keys on the explicit marker instead. The peer event carries no package, so the marker is also the only way a peer can drop exactly one package's slot of a type stored per `(package, name)`.
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx` (Lane 1): the payload code block and the receipt paragraph name `removal`. **Outside the claim's file surface.** The doc described the payload's whole shape, and this PR makes that description false, so os-dev.md rule 3 ("本轮改动令其变假…的已发布缺陷必修") requires the edit. Declared in the report.
- `.changeset/32499-peer-removal-door-copy.md`: `@objectstack/metadata` patch.

## Tests

`packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-cluster.test.ts` (the cluster harness): new top-level `describe` "a peer's removal deletes this node's in-memory (artifact door) copy too (#32499)". Each node has its own door `MemoryLoader`, booted as the ingest does: saved, then `register(…, { notify: false })`. All nodes share one store and one bus.

- `view` / `object` / `datasource` / `position` (#32353's census types): `unregister` on A, and B answers nothing at once (`list` / `get` / `exists`) from no loader. The other door item still answers on both nodes.
- Each of the 6 types stored per `(package, name)`, via `unregister(…, { packageId })` and `unregisterPackage`: B drops that package's slot and keeps the other package's.
- Negative pins:
  - the peer never deletes from the shared store;
  - CONTROL: a peer's update keeps B's door copy;
  - a `deleted` event with no `removal` keeps B's door copy answering;
  - a `removal` with a non-string package deletes nothing.
- Failure path: a by-name removal B's door cannot apply logs once at `error`.

<details><summary>Reverse verification: BASE metadata-manager.ts (3452dec2) under the new tests</summary>

`git restore --source=3452dec2 -- packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts`, then the file run: `Tests 16 failed | 28 passed (44)`. The red set is every positive pin: 4 by-name types, 6 slotted types, and 6 error-path pins. The 4 negative pins stayed green on BASE, as negatives should. Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- …`; blob `52437f41` equals `HEAD:` and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations, one per negative pin (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, WRAP mode; each restore proven: blob 52437f41 = HEAD, git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

- A1, drop on any named event (`if (p.event.name) …`): 8 red, including CONTROL "a peer's update … keeps its door copy" and "a `deleted` event that carries no removal …".
- A2, drop on `event.type === 'deleted'`: 7 red, including "a `deleted` event that carries no removal …".
- A3, peer deletes through `isRemovalTarget` (`datasource:` included): 1 red, "the shared store is the origin's to delete from".
- A4, a non-string package read as `{}`: 6 red, "a removal whose package is not a string is dropped" for each slotted type.
- A5, the peer also deletes by name after the package's slot: 6 red, "one package's removal on A — B drops that package's slot and keeps the other package's".

The first A1/A2 run left the unmarked-delete pin green. The shared store answered that read, so the pin was vacuous. It now runs with no shared store and asserts B's door directly. A1/A2 were re-run after that fix (numbers above).
</details>

Under the verify lock: `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/metadata^...' build`, then `BUILD_EXIT=0`, `TYPECHECK_EXIT=0` (`tsc --noEmit`, the tsconfig includes `src/**/*`, so the test file is compiled), and `Test Files 74 passed (74) · Tests 1427 passed (1427)`, `TEST_EXIT=0`.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- A removal made with `notify: false` publishes nothing, so it reaches no peer: neither the registry entry nor the door copy. Unchanged and pre-existing. Several first-party removal callers use it (#32493's census), and they converge peers through their own lanes or not at all.
- `resyncClusterPubSub()` after a bus outage drops list caches only. A removal hint lost in the outage leaves the peer's door copy, just as it already leaves the peer's registry entries. Unchanged.
- A reload or restart of the artifact still restores a door item on every node (#32493's documented recovery).
- In-flight same-package PRs read before push: #32533 touched `metadata-manager.ts` near `removalOf` and landed; it is merged here. #32569 touches the version-history range after `detachClusterPubSub`, and my hunks stay outside it.

## Verification

Readings at head `d0a5a29e` (branch tip after merging main `874166b6`), objectstack-ai/objectstack:

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 94 derived families. Every one ran locally with its exit captured before any pipe. `--ran` with `COMMAND :: exit CODE` reports: "94 derived, 94 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN" (a derived zero, none exit 3).
- 7 of the 94 first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3, nothing measured) on an unbuilt tree. They were re-run after the builds they name, and each reached exit 0: `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:doc-security-posture`, `check:docs-transcript-drift`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt` ("0 raw tsc error(s) total"), `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` ("122 published require entry point(s) across 72 package(s) load"), `check:skill-examples`.
- Among them: `check:durability-log-level` exit 0 (the peer's new `catch` around `deleteMetaItemFromLoader` logs at `error`), `check:nul-bytes` exit 0, `check:cross-package-test-inputs` exit 0, `check:doc-authoring` exit 0.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` over the two changed TS files: exit 0, no output. The repository-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI (`Lint & Repo Gates`).
- The ablations and the reverse verification ran on the pre-merge heads `582954d7` (A3, A4) and `c5fb24cd` (A1, A2, A5). The merge with main changed neither the test file nor the new hunks. The post-merge package run above covers the file at `d0a5a29e`.
